svg.text: Cribl Stream To Splunk — Components, Ports And Protocols

Every data path mutually authenticated with certificates, and both consoles are HTTPS. The one exception is marked and is a lab artifact: the leader-to-worker bundle channel takes TLS only when distributed settings come from instance.yml rather than environment variables.
SENDERS — THE ENVIRONMENT AS IT ALREADY IS
CRIBL STREAM — WORKER GROUP AND LEADER
SPLUNK ENTERPRISE
Windows hosts — universal forwarder
Security · System · Sysmon · Defender · AppLocker
outputs.conf tcpout → the worker, not the indexer
No new agent. The change is one file.
limits.conf maxKBps must not stay at 256.
Domain controllers
DNS Server / Analytical (ETW) · DHCP audit
DNS analytical renders as XML at ~1 KB a record —
one of the two largest feeds in most environments.
Network and security appliances
Palo Alto · Cisco ASA and ISE · Suricata · proxy
NetFlow / IPFIX collector
Syslog senders that cannot take an agent.
Point them at the worker's VIP, not one worker.
Cloud and application
Entra ID sign-in · container stdout · web tier
Collectors and HEC senders. Not every feed is
reduced — identity data is kept whole.
Client certificate on every sender.
The Source checks the common name, so a
certificate the CA signed is not sufficient on its own.
Worker group — every worker identical, no shared state
SOURCES
splunk (S2S) 9997/tcp TLS mutual
syslog 9514/tcp+udp TLS
tcpjson 10060/tcp TLS mutual
splunk_hec 8088/tcp TLS
compress: auto — the default rejects a forwarder
sending compressed = true, and it reads as a firewall.
ROUTES AND PIPELINES
one route per sourcetype, all final
drop · sample · mask · field strip
every pipeline sets the target index
catch-all writes to a FILE, not devnull
Cooked data skips index-time transforms on the
indexer, so the index must be right when it leaves.
DESTINATIONS
splunk_lb → indexers 9997/tcp S2S v4, TLS, client certificate
filesystem → unmatched capture, local disk
persistent queue on its own volume — never on /opt/cribl/state
A volume on /opt/cribl/state makes bundle apply a cross-device rename, which fails EXDEV.
The worker then keeps its last good config forever and still reports healthy.
One invalid Destination disables every Destination in the file, and the error names the wrong one.
Leader
UI and API 9000/tcp HTTPS, loopback only
config bundles 4200/tcp
Carries no data. Workers keep running
on last applied config if it is gone.
UI TLS is api.ssl in the leader's own cribl.yml,
not distributed.master, which the env vars override.
What the leader must not lose
auth/cribl.secret
It encrypts every stored Destination
credential. Back it up separately —
a leader rebuild without it loses them all,
and the UI comes back looking healthy.
Workers publish no host ports. Senders reach them over the network the workers are on, behind a VIP with a real health check —
never leastconn without one, which steers new connections toward the worker that is failing fastest.
Worker process count follows the CPU quota. Six processes on a one-CPU container is a slow outage that reads as healthy.
Both consoles are HTTPS and refuse plain http. Every data path is mutually authenticated TLS.
Indexer — receiver
[splunktcp-ssl://9997] TLS 1.2+
requireClientCert = 1
sslCommonNameToCheck names each sender
Never SPLUNK_ENABLE_LISTEN. It writes a plaintext
[splunktcp://9997] into the search app, a different
stanza that the TLS one never overrides.
Management and search
Splunk Web 8000/tcp HTTPS only
splunkd management 8089/tcp HTTPS
enableSplunkWebSSL, and nothing on port 80.
Indexes
win · net · identity · app
The index is set by the Cribl pipeline, not by a
transforms.conf rule on the indexer: index-time
transforms do not run on cooked S2S data, and
the rule fails silently rather than erroring.
outputs.conf must NOT carry selectiveIndexing on
an indexer — it discards everything, silently.
S2S v4 · mTLS
S2S v4 · mTLS
9514/tcp+udp
syslog · TLS
tcpjson · HEC
splunk_lb · S2S v4
cooked · mTLS
4200/tcp — the config bundle channel, and how to encrypt it
The bundle is the group's outputs.yml verbatim, so every Destination credential crosses this port once per worker,
on every deploy. Encrypt it by configuring distributed mode in local/_system/instance.yml with certPath and
privKeyPath. It cannot be done with CRIBL_DIST_MODE set: tls:// in the URL enables TLS with NO certificate, the
leader then binds nothing, workers sit at "sending is blocked", and both containers still report healthy.
Certificates
Generated outside the images, per host, and
mounted at a staging path. Splunk runs splunkd
as splunk, so a read-only mount at the final path
leaves 0600 keys unreadable and TLS silently off.
Acknowledgment
Cribl's Splunk S2S Source implements no indexer
acknowledgment — acks in Cribl are a HEC feature.
A forwarder set useACK = true against Cribl waits
for one that never comes. Durability is the PQ.
event data — mutually authenticated TLS
config bundle on 4200 — TLS needs instance.yml, not env vars
Operator access is not drawn: Splunk Web on 8000 and the Cribl UI on 9000 are HTTPS and bound to loopback, reached through a jump host rather than from this diagram's networks.
Ports shown are the defaults. Every one is configurable, and the numbers in use are a per-environment decision recorded at build.

Lab-verified on Splunk 10.4.2 and Cribl Stream 4.19.2: 9997 S2S mTLS · 8000 HTTPS · 8089 HTTPS · 9000 HTTPS, plain http refused on both consoles. 4200 is plaintext in this lab only, because distributed mode is set by environment variable.
Read from the shipped schemas rather than recalled: compress enum, splunk_lb key set, and the Source and Destination key sets that do not match each other.
